issues.body: The warning is emitted only inside `if not isinstance(item, dict)`. A row with a valid salted label but a present malformed `utilization_1h` (for example `"busy"`) passes that guard, `_obs_fraction` returns `None`, and the row is omitted from `lease_utilizations` without any diagnostic. If valid rows are alongside it, the code still publishes a confident mean/max over the survivors—the exact partial-sample failure described by this change. This is not hypothetical in the existing contract: the self-test fixture already includes an unparseable utilization and describes it as excluded from the aggregate. The new accept-path test contains only readable values, so it cannot detect this omission.
issues.fix_hint: Distinguish an absent/null utilization (if that remains an intentionally unmeasured row) from a present value that `_obs_fraction` cannot read, and send the latter through the lease drop log before continuing. Add a literal malformed-utilization case beside a valid row and assert both the survivor aggregate and the exact warning; also assert the intended behavior for missing/null utilization explicitly.
issues.title: Unreadable utilization rows are still silently removed from the aggregate

verdict.summary: The new diagnostic covers only non-object lease entries, so the same misleading partial-sample condition remains silent when a structurally valid lease row carries an unreadable utilization. Because the stated control is meant to announce rows subtracted from the published mean/max, this is an incomplete fix and the added tests do not exercise the remaining path.
